helloReact.title: The First Greeting
helloReact.desc: Render the text "Hello, React!" inside an h1 element.

docs.summary: JSX is the language of React's UI. It looks like HTML, but it lives inside JavaScript and compiles to React.createElement calls.

concepts.title: JSX elements
concepts.text:
Write tags like

…

inside your component. Tag names for HTML elements stay lowercase.

concepts.title: return
concepts.text:
A component must return JSX. Wrap multi-line returns in parentheses: return (

…

);

multipleElements.title: Twin Glyphs
multipleElements.desc: Return both an h1 ("Title") and a p ("Description") from one component.

docs.summary: A component can return only one root node. To return siblings, wrap them in a Fragment.

concepts.title: One root
concepts.text: return ( <h1/><p/> ) is invalid JSX. Adjacent elements need a parent.

concepts.title: Fragment
concepts.text: Use <>…</> (or <React.Fragment>) to group elements without adding an extra DOM node.

firstComponent.title: Birth of a Component
firstComponent.desc: Define a Greeting component and render it from App.

docs.summary: Components are functions that return JSX. They are the reusable building blocks of every React app.

concepts.title: Function components
concepts.text:
function Greeting() { return

Hello!

; } — names must start with a capital letter.

concepts.title: Using a component
concepts.text: Render it like an element: <Greeting />. React calls the function and inserts the returned JSX.

propsIntro.title: Gifts of the Props
propsIntro.desc: Build a UserCard that accepts name and role props and displays them.

docs.summary: Props are inputs you pass to a component, like attributes on an HTML tag. They flow one way: parent → child.

concepts.title: Passing props
concepts.text: <UserCard name="Alice" role="Developer" /> sends two string props to UserCard.

concepts.title: Reading props
concepts.text: Destructure them in the parameter list: function UserCard({ name, role }) { … }

dynamicContent.title: Living Expressions
dynamicContent.desc: Embed JavaScript expressions inside JSX to show dynamic values.

docs.summary: Curly braces { } open a portal from JSX into JavaScript. Anything inside is evaluated and rendered.

concepts.title: Expressions in JSX
concepts.text: Use {variable}, {1 + 2}, or {fn()} — any expression, not a full statement.

concepts.title: What renders
concepts.text: Numbers and strings appear as text. Booleans, null, and undefined render nothing.

conditionalRendering.title: Forks of Fate
conditionalRendering.desc: Show different UI depending on a condition.

docs.summary: Conditional rendering lets you show or hide parts of the UI based on data — like choosing a path at a crossroads.

concepts.title: Ternary
concepts.text: {isLoggedIn ? <Dashboard /> : <Login />} picks one of two branches.

concepts.title: Logical &&
concepts.text:
{hasError &&

Error

} renders the right side only when the left side is truthy.

listRendering.title: The March of Lists
listRendering.desc: Transform an array into a list of JSX elements with map.

docs.summary: Lists in React come from data. map() turns each item into an element you can render.

concepts.title: array.map
concepts.text:
items.map(item =>
  • {item}
    • ) returns an array of JSX that React renders in order.

concepts.title: key prop
concepts.text: Give each sibling a stable unique key (often an id) so React can track changes efficiently.

composition.title: Assembly of Allies
composition.desc: Split the UI into Header, Content, and Footer components and compose them in App.

docs.summary: Composition means building complex UIs from small components. Each piece focuses on one job.

concepts.title: Small components
concepts.text: Header, Content, and Footer each return their own JSX. App places them together.

concepts.title: Why compose
concepts.text: Smaller pieces are easier to read, reuse, and test than one giant component.

brokenCounter.title: The Broken Counter
brokenCounter.desc: Fix the counter so clicking updates the displayed number using useState.

docs.summary: Local variables do not survive re-renders and never tell React to update the screen. State does both.

concepts.title: useState
concepts.text: const [count, setCount] = useState(0) gives you the current value and a setter.

concepts.title: Updating state
concepts.text: Call setCount(newValue) (or setCount(prev => prev + 1)). React re-renders with the new value.

toggleSwitch.title: The Toggle Switch
toggleSwitch.desc: Use boolean state to toggle UI on and off.

docs.summary: Boolean state is perfect for switches, modals, and menus — anything that is either on or off.

concepts.title: Boolean useState
concepts.text: const [isOn, setIsOn] = useState(false) stores a true/false flag.

concepts.title: Toggling
concepts.text: setIsOn(!isOn) or setIsOn(prev => !prev) flips the value safely.

controlledInput.title: The Bound Input
controlledInput.desc: Make an input controlled: its value comes from state, updated on every change.

docs.summary: A controlled input is fully driven by React state. The input never holds its own secret value.

concepts.title: value + onChange
concepts.text: Bind value={text} and onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)} so state and input stay in sync.

concepts.title: Single source of truth
concepts.text: State owns the text. That makes validation, formatting, and sharing the value much easier.

formHandling.title: The Submission Scroll
formHandling.desc: Build a form with controlled name and email fields and handle submit.

docs.summary: Forms combine controlled inputs with an onSubmit handler. Always prevent the browser's default reload.

concepts.title: onSubmit
concepts.text: Put onSubmit on the <form>. Inside the handler, call e.preventDefault().

concepts.title: Multiple fields
concepts.text: Each field usually has its own piece of state (or one object state for the whole form).

liftingState.title: Raising the Shared Flame
liftingState.desc: Lift shared state so two sibling inputs stay synchronized.

docs.summary: When two children need the same data, move that state into their closest common parent and pass it down as props.

concepts.title: Lifting state up
concepts.text: The parent owns the state. Children receive values and setters (or callbacks) via props.

concepts.title: Single source
concepts.text: One piece of state means siblings cannot drift out of sync.

stateFromProps.title: The Initial Spark
stateFromProps.desc: Initialize state from a prop — knowing it only applies on the first render.

docs.summary: useState(propValue) uses the prop only as the initial value. Later prop changes do not automatically rewrite that state.

concepts.title: Initial state
concepts.text: const [text, setText] = useState(initialText) copies initialText once when the component mounts.

concepts.title: Props vs state
concepts.text: If you need to stay in sync with a changing prop, either derive during render or update with an effect — but for editable fields, local state from an initial prop is often correct.

dataFetcher.title: The Scrying Fetch
dataFetcher.desc: Fetch data on mount with useEffect and store it in state.

docs.summary: useEffect runs side effects after paint — perfect for fetching, subscriptions, and talking to the outside world.

concepts.title: Mount-only effect
concepts.text: useEffect(() => { … }, []) runs once after the first render because the dependency array is empty.

concepts.title: Fetch → state
concepts.text: Load data inside the effect, then setState with the result so the UI can display it.

cleanupEffect.title: The Cleanup Rite
cleanupEffect.desc: Set up an interval in useEffect and clean it up to avoid leaks.

docs.summary: Effects that start something ongoing (timers, listeners) must also stop it. Return a cleanup function from useEffect.

concepts.title: Cleanup function
concepts.text: return () => clearInterval(id) runs when the component unmounts or before the effect re-runs.

concepts.title: Why it matters
concepts.text: Without cleanup, intervals keep firing after the component is gone — memory leaks and ghost updates.

domReference.title: The Dom Mirror
domReference.desc: Use useRef to grab a DOM node and focus it.

docs.summary: useRef holds a mutable .current value that persists across renders without causing re-renders. With the ref prop, it points at a DOM element.

concepts.title: Creating a ref
concepts.text: const inputRef = useRef(null) creates the ref object.

concepts.title: Attaching & using
concepts.text: Put ref={inputRef} on an element, then call inputRef.current.focus() when you need the node.

customHook.title: Forge Your Own Hook
customHook.desc: Extract toggle logic into a reusable useToggle custom hook.

docs.summary: Custom hooks let you reuse stateful logic. They are ordinary functions whose names start with use and that may call other hooks.

concepts.title: Naming
concepts.text: Always start with use (useToggle, useFetch) so React's rules of hooks can apply.

concepts.title: Return what you need
concepts.text: Return a tuple or object — e.g. [value, toggle] — so components stay clean.

slotPattern.title: The Children Slot
slotPattern.desc: Build a Card that renders a title and its children content.

docs.summary: children is a special prop: whatever you place between opening and closing tags is passed in automatically.

concepts.title: children prop
concepts.text: function Card({ title, children }) receives nested JSX as children.

concepts.title: Slots
concepts.text: Render {children} where the content should appear — a flexible composition pattern.

renderProps.title: The Render Prop Pact
renderProps.desc: Use a render prop so the parent decides how to display shared mouse data.

docs.summary: A render prop is a function prop that returns JSX. The child calls it with data; the parent decides the UI.

concepts.title: Function as prop
concepts.text:
Pass render={(pos) =>

{pos.x}, {pos.y}

} (or use children as a function).

concepts.title: Inversion of control
concepts.text: The reusable component owns the behavior (tracking the mouse); the parent owns the presentation.
